• Option 1 (Sahi Jawab) — Jab acetone ya ethanol haath par lagaaya jaata hai, toh ye liquid molecules bahut rapidly evaporate hone lagte hain kyunki inki vapor pressure bahut high hoti hai. Evaporation ek endothermic process hai — yaani isme heat absorb hoti hai. Ye heat seedha hamare haath ki skin se li jaati hai (Latent Heat of Vaporization). Jab haath ki heat liquid mein transfer hoti hai evaporation ke liye, toh haath ka local temperature gir jaata hai aur hume thand ka ehsaas hota hai. Ye ek purely physical process hai — koi chemical reaction nahi.

• Option 0 (Galat) — Acetone ya ethanol skin lipids ke saath react karke 'ice crystals' nahi banate. Ice crystal formation ke liye temperature 0°C se neeche chahiye. Ye statement scientifically impossible hai aur ek deliberate examiner trap hai.

• Option 2 (Galat) — Solvents nerve impulses block nahi karte in small quantities. Nerve freezing ek pharmacological anesthetic phenomenon hai, koi evaporation cooling nahi.

• Option 3 (Galat) — Acetone ya ethanol CO2 absorb karke carbonate nahi banate. Ye chemically incorrect hai.

Memory tip: Volatile liquid + Skin = Evaporation → Latent heat skin se → Skin thandi. Yahi concept sweating mein bhi kaam karta hai!

qe: When ice-cold water is poured into a dry glass tumbler, a mist of liquid water droplets rapidly forms on the outer glass surface. What physical process causes these droplets to appear?
qh: जब बर्फ जैसे ठंडे पानी को एक सूखे कांच के गिलास में डाला जाता है, तो कांच की बाहरी सतह पर तरल पानी की बूंदों की धुंध तेजी से बनती है। कौन सी भौतिक प्रक्रिया इन बूंदों को दिखाई देने का कारण बनती है?
oe: Water molecules seeping directly through solid glass pores via osmosis.
Sublimation of glass silicon dioxide into water liquid.
Chemical oxidation of atmospheric nitrogen into liquid water.
Condensation of invisible atmospheric water vapor upon losing thermal energy when contacting the cold glass surface.
oh: परासरण (osmosis) द्वारा ठोस कांच के छिद्रों से सीधे पानी के अणुओं का रिसाव।
कांच के सिलिकॉन डाइऑक्साइड का जल तरल में ऊर्ध्वपातन।
वायुमंडलीय नाइट्रोजन का तरल पानी में रासायनिक ऑक्सीकरण।
ठंडी कांच की सतह के संपर्क में आने पर तापीय ऊर्जा खोने पर अदृश्य वायुमंडलीय जलवाष्प का संघनन।
e:
Thande paani ka glass bahar se geela kyun ho jaata hai — ye ek classic daily life observation hai jiska science exam mein baar baar explanation maanga jaata hai. Iska answer Condensation ke concept mein hai.

Sabse pehle ek important background fact: Hamari atmosphere mein hamesha kuch na kuch water vapor (gaseous form mein paani) present rehta hai — ise atmospheric humidity kehte hain. Ye vapor aankh se nahi dikh ta.

• Option 1 (Sahi Jawab) — Jab thande paani wala glass bahar ki garm, humid air ke sampark mein aata hai, toh glass ki outer surface bahut thandi hoti hai. Jab atmosphere ka warm water vapor is thandi glass surface ke paas aata hai, toh vapor ke molecules ki kinetic energy (heat) glass surface mein transfer ho jaati hai. Molecules ki kinetic energy kam hone se unki speed ghatti hai aur wo gas state se liquid state mein aa jaate hain — ise Condensation kehte hain. Ye condensed liquid droplets glass ki baahri surface par jama ho jaate hain aur hume 'mist' ya 'sweat' jaisa dikhta hai. Ye paani glass ke andar se nahi aaya — ye atmosphere se aaya hai!

• Option 0 (Sabse bada trap!) — Solid glass ek non-porous amorphous solid hai. Osmosis sirf semi-permeable membranes mein hota hai, solid glass mein nahi. Ye statement physically impossible hai aur ek classic examiner trap hai jo students ko confuse karta hai.

• Option 2 (Galat) — Atmospheric nitrogen (N2) normal conditions par paani mein oxidize nahi hota. N2 ek inert gas hai. Ye statement chemically baseless hai.

• Option 3 (Galat) — Glass (SiO2) ka sublimation normal room temperatures par nahi hota — iske liye thousands of degrees Celsius chahiye. Aur SiO2 liquid water nahi banta. Ye ek deliberately absurd option hai.

Yaad rakhein: Bahar ki water vapor → Thandi glass surface → Heat loss → Condensation → Liquid droplets. Yahi process AC rooms ki outer walls aur cold drink bottles par bhi hoti hai!
